evidence.claim: The 12.5 miles inside the reservation received state scenic-byway designation on June 27, 1996, followed by national designation on July 15.
evidence.quote: 12.5 miles (20.1 km) of the route (the entirety of the route within the Pyramid Lake Indian Reservation) became a Nevada Scenic Byway on June 27, 1996. The same stretch was designated a National Scenic Byway on July 15 of that same year.

evidence.quote: The Pyramid (39°58′48″N 119°30′06″W), also known as Fremont's Pyramid and Pyramid Island, is a small island near the southeastern shore of the lake.

evidence.quote: It is located approximately 1.2 miles (2 km) northeast of Anaho Island and slightly less than six miles (9.5 km) from the community of Sutcliffe.

evidence.quote: The English name of the lake, given to it by explorer John C. Frémont, comes from the impressive cone- or pyramid-shaped tufa formations found in the lake and along the shores.

flags: Current copy equated the whole byway with the 12.5-mile SR 445 segment. FHWA lists 30.2 miles, and the SR 447 page includes portions of SR 446 and SR 447. The catalog’s 41.9 miles describes the whole numbered SR 445, not the scenic segment.

The strip data has nonmonotonic mile entries for Sutcliffe, Wadsworth and Nixon and cannot establish a single through-drive. Copy explicitly uses a southbound west-shore drive then the SR 446 connection to Nixon.

All current landmarks, exact titles, coordinates and motifs are retained. The Pyramid and Anaho Island are offshore subjects ordered north to south before Sutcliffe; their retained island coordinates are not visitor access points. The cache does not establish specific roadside viewpoints.

Replaced the broad current north/east-shore closure and general day-use permit wording with the Tribe’s named closures and explicit swimming/camping permit requirement. No stale FHWA price or Wikipedia-only boat setback is presented as current guidance.
The tribal site and Wikipedia give different lake areas, so acreage is omitted. Secondary pages vary in Paiute-language name spellings; only the Tribe’s English name and Cui-ui spelling are used.
